title: Brioche rib baby blanket
subtitle: A lofty 75 by 90 cm cot blanket in one-colour brioche on 5 mm needles.
excerpt: A 75 by 90 cm cot blanket worked flat in one-colour brioche rib on 5 mm needles. Brioche produces a deep, squishy fabric twice as thick as stocking stitch from the same weight yarn. About 350 g of DK in brioche creates an aran-weight-equivalent drape.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 9th series (1893), §Brioche or Tuck Stitch, describes one-colour brioche as a warm blanket fabric, noting its doubled thickness. Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), §Brioche Knitting, documents the slip-yarn-over setup row and the brk / brp abbreviations.

knitting.gaugeText: 16 sts × 28 brioche rows = 10 × 10 cm in one-colour brioche on 5 mm needles (each brioche row = 2 passes). The fabric relaxes considerably after the first wash.

stitchCountCheckpoints.label: Halfway check — 120 sts on needle (working sts only), about 45 cm

glossaryTerms.definition: The right-side stitch in one-colour brioche. Insert the right needle through both the slipped stitch and the yarn-over from the previous row and knit them together as one stitch. Produces the raised knit column visible on the right side.

The alternating stitch in brioche flat knitting. Bring the yarn to the front, slip the next stitch purlwise, then bring the yarn over the needle to the back — this paired slip-yarn-over is treated as a single unit on the next row.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat on 5 mm needles in one-colour
brioche
rib, finishing at 75 cm wide by 90 cm long.

Single-panel construction; no seaming. Brioche rib was chosen because its doubled structure creates a fabric twice as thick as stocking stitch: a DK yarn in brioche on 5 mm needles produces a blanket as warm as chunky-weight garter at similar weight and yardage. The larger needle size accommodates the doubled structure without tightness. Budget about 350 g (about 770 m / 840 yards) of DK. Note: one brioche row is two passes of the needle; row counts in this pattern refer to passes.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 350 g (about 770 m / 840 yards) of DK-weight yarn. A smooth merino DK shows brioche texture best.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 5 mm (UK 6 / US 8) circular needle, 80 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge

16 stitches and 28 brioche rows (= 56 passes) to 10 cm over one-colour brioche on 5 mm needles. Brioche gauge is very different from stocking-stitch gauge on the same needle. Swatch in brioche for at least 12 cm before casting on; the stitch count appears halved in brioche because each column involves one working stitch and one slip-yo pair.
If your stitch gauge is 14 per 10 cm with 120 stitches, the blanket will be about 86 cm wide instead of 75 cm. Adjust the cast-on count in multiples of 2.
Stitches used

items.name: brk
items.qty: brioche knit: k the slipped st and its yo together

items.name: sl1yo
items.qty: slip 1 purlwise, yarn over, the setup stitch for brioche purl

items.name: brp
items.qty: brioche purl: bring yarn front, sl1yo

content.text: Pattern
Cast-on
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 120 stitches (a multiple of 2). Long-tail tail: (5 × 120) / 10 + 15 = 60 + 15 = 75 cm. Measure 90 cm of tail.
Setup row
Row 0 (WS setup): *sl1yo, k1; repeat from * to end. This row sets up the slip-yo pairs for the first brioche row.
Body
Row A (RS): k1, *brk, sl1yo; rep from * to last st, k1.
Row B (WS): k1, *sl1yo, brp; rep from * to last st, k1.
Alternate rows A and B until the blanket measures 90 cm. When you set this aside, note whether the next row is A (RS) or B (WS).
Stitch count check-ins

At pass 126 (about 45 cm, note: counting passes not rows): count the stitches on the needle. You should have 120 working stitches plus 120 yarn-overs paired with them, for 240 loops total; or count only the non-yo stitches, which should be 120. At pass 250 (about 89 cm): count again before casting off.
Common faults
Brk worked into only the slip stitch without the yo, producing a tight column: the yarn-over was dropped or missed. After each sl1yo, confirm the loop is on the right needle before proceeding.

Setup row lost after putting the work down: on a restart, if uncertain which row is next, check the RS face, brk stitches present as prominent raised Vs. If the next stitch shows a raised V, the next row is B (WS).
Cast-off

Use a brioche-specific cast-off or a loose standard cast-off. Standard cast-off: work a brk (or brp as appropriate), then pass the previous stitch over. Work the cast-off row with needles one size larger than the blanket needles to prevent a tight edge.
Finishing
Weave in both ends along a brioche column. The fabric will spring open after the first wash; do not block flat before washing.
Care
Hand wash in cool water or machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle for superwash DK. Lay flat to dry. Brioche fabric is bouncy; it will spring back to its relaxed width after drying.
What to try next

From one-colour brioche, try two-colour brioche next. Each row uses a different yarn colour. The result is a reversible fabric where the RS and WS show opposite colour schemes. The stitches are the same; you add a colour-change step at each row.
